the phylogenetic analyses of Euphylla and Fimbriapilla species revealed the paraphyly of Euphylliidae, and the dichotomy of polyp morphology, reproductive traits, colony form, and skeletal morphology of the species in Euphylla, Fimbriapillia, and Galaxea is a convergent trait.
the genus Euphylllia (Scleractinia) is paraphyletic, with the subgenus Fimbriaphillia being a distinct genus.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phylogenetic analyses of Euphylla and Fimbriophyllia revealed that polyp morphology, colony structure, and reproductive traits have a greater impact on their systematics than skeletal morphology.
the dichotomy of colony structure in the Euphylidae (V) has been resolved and that the genus Fimbriaphyilla has been resurrected from a subgenus.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of multiple traits in phylogenetic analyses will improve our understanding of the systematics of scleractinians and, by extension other corals, and will help resolve the evolutionary history of scleractinia.
the dichotomy in the colony structure is a convergent trait and that the dichotomy is better defined by polyp features, life history traits, and skeletal structure.
soft-tissue morphology, reproductive mode, and colony structure are of high systematic value in the scleractinians.
